newsitem.title: CROATIA: Ericsson Croatia says to boost sales, rationalise.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson Croatia says to boost sales, rationalise.

text.p: Telecommunications equipment maker Ericsson Nikola Tesla, a Croatian subsidiary of Sweden's Ericsson, said on Friday it hoped to boost output and rationalise business to increase profitability.
"We are aiming for expansion in 1997...with a 10 percent increase in physical output and sales," company president Per Olof Sjoestedt told Reuters during an investment conference.
He said sales were alrady up 10 percent this year from some 200 million German marks in 1995 but added:
"Our concerns are relatively high assets and number of employees in relation with sales. We are planning to attack it by increasing sales and reducing staff."
With 3.5 percent of the group's total workforce, the Croatian unit was contributing to sales with only one percent.
It planned no investments into the existing production lines but would rather spend 5-6 percent of its turnover on computerisation, Sjoestedt said.
The exports, representing some 60 percent of total sales this year, would remain on the same level in 1997.
Last year, Ericsson Nikola Tesla had a net profit of 68.6 million kuna, but Sjoestedt made no forecast for this year. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
